chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
title: Prize fights at San Jacinto and young Polite
summary: Sunday fights; fighter Young Polite and trainer Albert Greger, and how Polite left for California.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And then the price fired every Sunday. You see, better fight there for that little fifteen and twenty cents. Yeah. And it went up to a quarter a little later and then you see now for fifty dollars. Yeah.
That was all year round they had prize fighters?
And all the members could go. And you see, after a fighter would get married there, then they could go fight at the Coliseum. Oh, I see.
Yeah, that's how that little kid got married there, Polite.
And the fat leather kid, John.

Yeah. But if Polite would have listened at me, he might have got round the championship. You know he wouldn't have listened at some of them boys there, man, don't stay here, you can make money after that. Do you know if he'd listen to Albert Greger he would have. Yeah, that's what I'm saying now. That other gang took him, persuaded him to go away, and he went out there and fight. A boy out there would have had a little bit more experience than him. Hard knock. A little Filipino. He was Mexican. That Mexican. Yeah, Mexican, that's right.

Young Polite? You see Albert Greger had a lot of fighters. Apparently he was a good trainer. And when he came in, I used to go by little Beck or Claiborne. Yeah. I mean, he was going to have lunch at 12 o'clock. And Albert told Polite, well I see y'all in the morning at the club, you know, to work out. Him and Benny left that night and went back to California to fight that match. Yeah, yeah. And Albert told him, you know, let him shape him up in about three months, maybe six months, he can go down and whip him. Because when he hit you. Yeah.
Al? He wasn't from New Orleans? Yeah, Polite was from New Orleans. Oh, he was from New Orleans. But he went to California.
Right there. Right there. Right around the corner of Biller Street. Yeah, he used to live right there.
